name: NVIDIA Rubin Ultra Kyber rack (NVL576 / NVL144)
model: Vera Rubin Ultra in Kyber rack (announced as NVL576 counting GPU dies; now NVL144 counting packages)
availability: Roadmap: H2 2027 (SemiAnalysis reported a slip to 2028 in July 2026; NVIDIA says its roadmap is intact)
description: Roadmap entry; most values are estimates. Kyber rotates compute blades vertically like books: GTC 2026 showed 2 chassis x 18 compute sleds, each with 4 Rubin Ultra GPU packages (4 reticle dies, 1 TB HBM4e each) and 2 Vera CPUs, i.e. 144 packages / 576 dies in one NVLink 7 domain. Rear NVLink switch blades plug into a passive midplane instead of cable cartridges. Power is 800 V DC only (NVIDIA: 54 V in-rack distribution hits physical limits above ~200 kW; it showed an 800 V sidecar powering 576 Rubin Ultra GPUs in one Kyber rack at GTC 2025): an adjacent power sidecar rectifies 415/480 V AC to 800 V DC; the APC sidecar shown at GTC 2026 held 7 x 3U 110 kW 800 V power shelves, 4 x 2U DC output PDUs, a 4U power management controller and 5 Li-ion battery backup units. The footprint here treats the compute rack plus its power sidecar as one placed unit (about two 600 mm slots). Cooling is all-liquid via the facility TCS through a CDU; NVIDIA has not published whether a cooling sidecar is used.

nominal_power_w.note: NVIDIA presented Kyber as a ~600 kW rack at GTC 2025 (press report). The GTC 2026 design looks half as dense (144 packages instead of 576), and NVIDIA did not restate power; one analyst suspects closer to 300 kW. 600 kW kept as the planning figure; override when NVIDIA publishes.

peak_power_w.note: no EDPp published; set to the N capacity of the GTC 2026 sidecar (6 of 7 x 110 kW shelves = 660 kW)

power_shelves.note: blog report of the APC 800 VDC sidecar at GTC 2026: 7 x 3U 110 kW shelves (6+1). Shelves sit in the sidecar, not the compute rack; the rack on display also seemed to have ~8 integrated shelves.

shelf_rating_w.note: blog report: 3U 110 kW 800 Vdc power shelves in the sidecar

liquid_fraction.note: press reports describe all-liquid cooling; Vera Rubin NVL72 trays are already 100% liquid-cooled. Sidecar rectifier losses may go to air. No vendor figure.

max_coolant_supply_c.note: assumed same 45 C inlet as Vera Rubin NVL72; not published for Kyber

width_mm.note: compute rack (assumed 600 mm MGX-class width) plus 800 VDC power sidecar (assumed 600 mm); NVIDIA publishes no Kyber dimensions

depth_mm.note: assumed same 1,200 mm planning depth as Vera Rubin NVL72; not published

height_mm.note: assumed same ~2,300 mm as Vera Rubin NVL72; not published

weight_kg.note: not published; expect well above Vera Rubin NVL72 (~1,800 kg) plus a sidecar with batteries. Get structural sign-off before planning.

feet.note: assumed four leveling feet each for compute rack and sidecar

scale_out_ports.note: GTC 2025 NVL576 figure was 115.2 TB/s ConnectX-9 (= 1,152 x 800G, press). The GTC 2026 sleds show 2 or 4 NICs each, so the count may be half. Expressed in 800G ports.

port_speed_gbps.note: ConnectX-9 1.6 Tb/s NICs modeled as 2 x 800G ports, as on Vera Rubin NVL72

scale_up_domain.note: 144 Rubin Ultra packages (576 dies) in one NVLink domain; NVIDIA's 2025 blog says 576 Rubin Ultra GPUs, counting dies

scale_up_bandwidth_tbps.note: press report of GTC 2025 figure: 1.5 PB/s NVLink 7 for NVL576 = 12,000 Tb/s; may change with the GTC 2026 redesign

network.port_media: OSFP-class front ports (ConnectX-9); details not published

accelerators.note: press report: 144 Rubin Ultra packages per system (4 compute dies each = 576 dies, the 'NVL576' count)

compute.accelerator_model: NVIDIA Rubin Ultra (4 reticle dies, 1 TB HBM4e)

cpus.note: 36 sleds x 2 Vera CPUs (blog report of GTC 2026 hardware)

hbm_tb.note: press report: 1 TB HBM4e per Rubin Ultra x 144. NVIDIA's 365 TB 'fast memory' figure includes CPU LPDDR.

fp4_pflops.note: press report: 15 EF FP4 (100 PF per GPU), an inference (sparse-basis) figure. Dense not published; ~10.5 EF if the Vera Rubin dense/inference ratio (2,520/3,600) holds.
